I will keep the land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. In Quzhou County, this is the main grain system, most rain comes in the summer maize season, and irrigation pressure is heavier on winter wheat, so this rotation fits my water, labor, and habit best. I would not split much land into cash crops this year because I am 59, I want a system I know well, I can manage it on time, and I want steady grain rather than higher risk. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, keep fertilizer at a moderate but productive level, irrigate wheat several times but maize only once if needed, and do a simple, mechanical field schedule: wheat with rotary tillage before sowing, then maize with no-tillage direct seeding right after wheat harvest to save time and preserve moisture. My target is a solid, realistic yield, not an extreme one.

Basis I used for this decision: Quzhou is a typical North China Plain winter wheat and summer maize area, with more than 80% of fields in that annual rotation and most rainfall falling in the maize season; local and provincial reports also emphasize this system and recent Quzhou demonstrations in wheat-maize production.
